title: 'The health system in Nepal is not prepared for this' - NPR
description: 'The health system in Nepal is not prepared for this'  NPR
publisher.title: NPR
full_article:
Transcript

AILSA CHANG, HOST:

It's been more than a week since catastrophic floods hit Nepal and Tibet. More than 1,200 people are reported dead, and more than 5,000 are still missing as crews keep searching for survivors. While the waters have receded, NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports that threats to physical and mental health persist.

JONATHAN LAMBERT, BYLINE: Before the floods, Bidur, in the Nuwakot District, was a bustling place. Hundreds of homes and businesses hugged the Trishuli River, which cuts a winding path through the Himalayas. Sushma Bhusal, of the humanitarian nonprofit IFRC, says the town was a central transit point, and she was stunned by what she saw in parts of it earlier this week.

SUSHMA BHUSAL: There's nothing left there. There's no village. There's no sign of anyone there. And a lot of houses have been, like, just washed off.

LAMBERT: Across the river, she says Trishuli Hospital was where many in the region sought care, but the flood destroyed the bridges that enabled many to reach it. While it once took 10 minutes to cross...

BHUSAL: Now, it takes about 10 hours for people to go and walk through the trail and get to the other side of the river.

LAMBERT: It's a situation that's playing out across the region and imperiling the health of tens of thousands. Floods have completely destroyed or damaged at least seven hospitals and health centers and cut off access to many more. That's making it harder to care for those injured by the floods and those with routine medical needs. Abhilasha Gurung is with UNICEF in Nepal.

ABHILASHA GURUNG: We know in the community there are pregnant women who have expected delivery date coming in the next few weeks. So we set up a basic medical tent so that health services can resume.

LAMBERT: Even health facilities that are mostly intact are still having problems like basic refrigeration for medical supplies.

GURUNG: There is no electricity. The vaccines are quickly started to degrade.

LAMBERT: Many who need medicine for chronic conditions can't get it now, either. Padam Simkhada is from this region and is now a global health researcher at the University of Chester in England.

PADAM SIMKHADA: People with diabetes, hypertension, cancer or other disease, they need a medication. And then even they survive because they run away, they lost the medication. There's no health facility to get that medicine. The consequences are the people who are already under chronic condition even become worse.

LAMBERT: Officials are scrambling to shore up this basic medical care. At the same time, they're on the lookout for new threats. Damaged water systems raise the risk of waterborne disease outbreaks like diarrhea or cholera, and thousands who have been displaced by the floods are crowded into temporary shelters, like gyms or government buildings, where airborne diseases can easily spread.

SIMKHADA: The health system in Nepal is not prepared for this level of disaster.

LAMBERT: There's also a mental health crisis brewing. Ayush Joshi, with the nonprofit Save the Children, visited a holding center earlier this week. He was struck by what happened whenever a helicopter looking for survivors passed overhead.

AYUSH JOSHI: You would see children in these holding center looking up in the sky, you know? And it's not just one child. It's, like, every child. They just look up.

LAMBERT: He says the kids looked hopeful.

JOSHI: Because every helicopter carries, even for a moment, the possibility that someone they love might be found.

LAMBERT: Many in these centers are holding on to that hope and struggling to come to terms with what's been lost.

JOSHI: One girl that I spoke to told me that she could not sleep because she had seen four of her best friends being washed away by the flood.

LAMBERT: Save the Children and other responders are trying to provide support now for acute psychological distress. But he says many of these mental scars will linger long after the official response ends.

Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.

title: Tennessee nonprofit confirms one Tennessean among 22 Americans still missing in Nepal - WTVC
description: Tennessee nonprofit confirms one Tennessean among 22 Americans still missing in Nepal  WTVC
publisher.title: WTVC
full_article:
CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. — Nine days after catastrophic flooding swept through northern Nepal, a Tennessee-based nonprofit has confirmed one Tennessean was among the 22 Americans traveling with its group who remain missing.

Isha Foundation instructor Allison Murray told us Thursday the organization is keeping the identities of those travelers private out of respect for their families.

"There is one Tennessean that was on the trip," Murray said. "The 22 that I know of, they're from different states."

It's the first confirmation we've received that a Tennessee resident was among the Americans traveling with the Isha Foundation group when disaster struck.

The Isha Foundation's McMinnville center tells us, among the 80 travelers on the way to Mount Kailash when the devastating Nepal flooding hit 9 days ago, one traveler came from Tennessee.

We first reported last week that nearly 80 people from 19 countries were traveling with the organization on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash when catastrophic flooding hit the region.

Isha Foundation has a major U.S. center in McMinnville, Tennessee.

The group included 22 Americans, but until now, it wasn't clear whether any of them were Tennessee residents.

Murray has been with the McMinnville center since it opened in 2006 and has made the Mount Kailash pilgrimage herself.

TRISHULI, NEPAL - AUGUST 27: A rescuer assists a resident through heavy mud following flash floods on August 27, 2026 in Trishuli, Nepal. A sudden flood swept through the Bhote Koshi River basin in northern Rasuwa on August 26, damaging settlements, roads and energy infrastructure as rescue teams searched for residents and foreign travellers reported out of contact. Hundreds were reported missing, as the death toll started to climb. (Photo by Ezra Acayan/Getty Images)

She says Isha Foundation has been making the journey for 21 years and has never experienced anything comparable.

"This is not a flood," Murray said. "This is a catastrophe of unparalleled proportions. Really, no one could anticipate something like this."

Mount Kailash is a sacred site for several religious traditions, and Murray says participants often spend years saving and preparing for the roughly three-week journey.

The trip also takes travelers to elevations of 15,000 to 16,000 feet, requiring medical screening and physical preparation before they leave.

But Murray says the missing Isha group had already completed that difficult portion of its journey.

She says they were no longer at high altitude and were crossing the border when the foundation lost contact with them.

TOPSHOT - A woman walks among the ruins of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district on September 1, 2026. The huge wave of freezing water and debris, sparked by a glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border, killed at least 939 people and left nearly 4,500 missing, with Kathmandu warning reconstruction costs could run into the "billions of dollars". (Photo by Arun SANKAR / AFP via Getty Images)

According to Murray, the group's leaders routinely check in as they move through different stages of the pilgrimage.

The last contact came as the travelers reached an immigration facility.

"They're closing out. They're done," Murray said. "Essentially, they finished, and that was the last contact they had with them."

Murray says concern grew almost immediately when the group's leader failed to make an expected call after crossing to the Nepali side of the border.

She says Isha Foundation later worked with government officials to confirm through passport records that the travelers had reached the immigration building.

"They were able to confirm, yes, they were all there in the building," Murray said.

The disaster has taken a personal toll at the McMinnville center.

Murray says she knew several of the missing travelers, including some she considers close friends.

"It's definitely a whirlwind. It's still a little hard to take in," Murray said. "Some people I knew better than others, but I've been around for many years, so a few of these people are close friends."

NUWAKOT, NEPAL - AUGUST 28: An Aerial view shows debris and mud covering settlements following flash floods on August 28, 2026 in DevGhat village, Nepal. Authorities said the flash floods were triggered after a mass of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river near the Nepal-China border, leaving hundreds dead or missing and causing widespread damage in affected districts. Authorities continued the gruelling search for victims, many buried under metres of mud, as both China and Nepal issued fresh flooding alerts. (Photo by Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images)

Isha Foundation says it has operated a hotline since shortly after the disaster and volunteers are supporting the missing travelers' families with food, emotional support and other needs.

The organization is not asking for donations for itself.

Murray says people who want to help should instead consider established organizations supporting rescue and recovery efforts in Nepal, where communities beyond the missing pilgrimage group have suffered enormous losses.

She says some of the Sherpas who have worked with Isha Foundation over the years lost family members and homes in the flooding.

"One of them continued to support us even after he'd lost everything," Murray said. "They're just extraordinary people."

Search and recovery operations are continuing in the region.

And Murray says support will still be needed long after the immediate disaster fades from attention.

"After this leaves the news cycle, it'll continue for people for quite some time," she said. "All of the recovery for them, emotionally, physically and otherwise."

title: ‘They’ll be finding bodies next year’: a renowned forensic scientist on Nepal’s ‘extreme challenges’ - theguardian.com
description: ‘They’ll be finding bodies next year’: a renowned forensic scientist on Nepal’s ‘extreme challenges’  theguardian.com
publisher.title: theguardian.com
full_article:
The bodies of some of those killed in the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster may never be found, and some of those that are may never be identified, a world-renowned forensic scientist says.

Prof Richard Bassed, the head of forensic medicine at Melbourne’s Monash University, spent three months in Thailand after the 2004 Boxing Day tsunami and also helped to identify victims of Victoria’s catastrophic Black Saturday bushfires in 2009.

Now he has watched as authorities in Nepal and Tibet struggle to find and identify the dead amid the agonies of the living after last week’s devastating flash flood. More than 1,250 people have been confirmed dead, with more than 5,000 missing.

Prakrit has already lost her father. As Nepal’s morgues fill, she hopes her DNA can be used to find her mother Read more

The difficult terrain, and inadequate communications and resources, would all hamper efforts, Bassed says.

“They could be washed anywhere, buried under mud. I imagine there’s a number they’ll never find. I imagine they’ll be finding bodies next year.”

Authorities are still finding bodies from the 2011 Japanese tsunami, he says.

The bodies from the 2004 tsunami were relatively easy to recover, but it still took a year to identify 5,000 people, he says.

“And there were still some we couldn’t identify.”

Asked how he copes with the horror of death on such a scale, he says he has “never found it long-term traumatising”.

“Occasionally you’ll see something that’ll hit close to home. For me, it’s kids,” he says.

“And the randomness. The randomness of a tsunami, the randomness of this massive flood. That gets to you.

“But mostly you have your clinical face on, you do the best you can and know you’re doing it to help people.”

Authorities will use rapidly improving DNA techniques to try to identify the victims. This week Nepali police urged relatives of missing tourists to provide “a fresh blood sample for DNA profiling and two passport-sized photographs” to the pathology laboratory at the police hospital in Kathmandu.

But authorities in Nepal and Tibet face “extreme challenges”, Bassed says.

They include the danger of more mudslides, the complexity of co-ordinating across international borders and the likelihood of local mortuaries and other infrastructure being overwhelmed by the number of bodies.

The mix of nations and religions also brings issues of different cultural beliefs around how and whether people should be buried.

The International Committee of the Red Cross and other international bodies have published Management of dead bodies after disasters: A field manual for First Responders to help people deal with bodies in a “proper and dignified way”, including by taking down details that will later help experts identify the remains.

First responders – often locals who are not forensic experts – are trained to follow those guidelines, tagging bodies in the hope they will later be matched to a missing person.

They give each body a unique code (for example the name of the place, the name of the team and a number). They will also take photos of the body and any distinguishing features such as gold teeth, clothing and tattoos, including that code in the image.

View image in fullscreen ‘You have your clinical face on, you do the best you can’ … Prof Richard Bassed. Photograph: John Lloyd Fillingham / Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine

Then they place the body in a body bag and organise its “orderly temporary storage”, again marked with the body code.

In Nepal, morgues are filling up and mass burials are taking place, as authorities collect DNA samples.

Bassed says most of the missing Australians would have dental records, which could help to identify them, but in Nepal many matches will be made using DNA or pictures, as fingerprints will often no longer be usable.

Work is under way to use AI and facial recognition technology to identify victims after disasters, but it’s controversial – Ukraine used Clearview AI software after the Russian invasion in 2022, just as the company was fined millions of dollars for collecting images of people in the UK and elsewhere without consent. Widespread use is also limited by access to the technology.

Bassed says researchers have also worked to devise an algorithm that could use passport or driver’s licence photos to identify someone.

“But it’s really complex, and it depends how they look, the trauma,” he says.

Another possibility is CT scanning, which can get a serial number from joint replacements, for example.

“But trying to get this technology to the places it’s needed in the middle of a disaster … you need running water, you need electricity … you could put CT scanners into helicopters, but all this costs an awful lot of money.”

आपदा के बाद पीड़ित के पहचान करै लेली एआई आरू फेशियल रिकग्निशन टेक्नोलॉजी के इस्तेमाल के काम चलै छै, लेकिन ई विवादित छै – यूक्रेन न॑ 2022 म॑ रूसी आक्रमण के बाद क्लियरव्यू एआई सॉफ्टवेयर के इस्तेमाल करलकै, ठीक वैसने जइसे कंपनी प॑ बिना सहमति के यूके आरू अन्य जगहऽ प॑ लोगऽ के तस्वीर इकट्ठा करै के कारण लाखों डॉलर के जुर्माना लगैलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । व्यापक उपयोग सेहो एहि तकनीक तक पहुंच क कारण सीमित अछि।

बेसड के कहनाय छनि जे शोधकर्ता एकटा एहन एल्गोरिदम बनेबा मे सेहो काज केलखिन्ह जे पासपोर्ट या ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस के फोटो के इस्तेमाल करि ककरो पहचान क सकय.

ओ कहैत छथि, “मुदा ई सचमुच जटिल अछि, आ ई निर्भर करैत अछि जे ओ केहन लगैत छथि, आघात पर.”

एकटा आओर संभावना अछि सीटी स्कैनिंग, जे उदाहरण के लेल जोड़ बदलय सं सीरियल नंबर ल सकैत अछि.

“मुदा कोनो आपदा के बीच एहि तकनीक के जरूरत के जगह पर पहुंचेबाक कोशिश मे... बहैत पानि चाही, बिजली चाही... हेलीकॉप्टर मे सीटी स्कैनर लगा सकैत छलहुं, मुदा एहि सब पर भयंकर पैसा खर्च होइत अछि.”

title: ‘Everyone seems to have forgotten’: In Tibet, flood-hit families search for the missing and grapple with China’s silence - theguardian.com
description: ‘Everyone seems to have forgotten’: In Tibet, flood-hit families search for the missing and grapple with China’s silence  theguardian.com
publisher.title: theguardian.com
full_article:
F an Hong last heard from her husband on the morning of the Nepal-Tibet disaster. More than a week later, the 31-year-old is desperately searching for information about Lin Bo, who was working on a Chinese highway project in Nepal. Struggling to get information from authorities, Fan turned to social media for help.

“My husband works on a project in Nepal, about 5 kilometres from the Gyirong border crossing. I want to know what the situation is, but I haven’t been able to reach him,” the 31-year-old from China’s Sichuan province wrote on Rednote.

Her post has gained more than 18,000 likes and nearly 4,600 comments. She is one of many in China with missing loved ones trying to piece together information they are finding online, as Tibetan advocate groups say information is being suppressed on that side of the border.

View image in fullscreen A screen outside a shopping mall in Beijing shows a news report featuring rescue workers at in Gyirong county. Photograph: Greg Baker/AFP/Getty Images

Lin began working on repairing the Syaphrubesi-Rasuwagadhi Highway – which links Nepal to Tibet, China, through the Gyirong border crossing – in 2024. He had been living on site and working on a 16km stretch of the road.

Fan says that rescue missions into the construction site have stalled. She says relatives of survivors are asking the Chinese authorities for permission to send up their own drones or helicopters to look for the missing.

“I feel more disheartened with each passing day. Feel colder and colder inside,” she told the Guardian. “I don’t even have any tears left.”

It is just over a week since the collapse of a glacier triggered devastating floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, destroying entire villages and killing more than 1,200 people. On Wednesday, 4,216 remained missing, according to Nepal officials. Chinese authorities say 541 remain unaccounted for on the Tibetan side, including 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries.

The relatively low official death toll from the Chinese authorities has also raised some concern among Tibetan advocacy groups, given the scale of the destruction seen in video footage. “All we can do is imagine – and that should terrify us,” said Tenzin Choekyi from Tibet Watch. As of Thursday, China had officially reported 21 people killed.

While in China, the official narrative heavily focuses on rescue efforts, online posts across Chinese social media show an emotional outpouring of grief and mourning. On Douyin, China’s version of TikTok, photographs of missing border inspection officers are shared under the hashtag “Salute to heroes guarding the nation’s gateway”.

In China, families with missing loved ones say they are relying on information from Nepal, as well as foreign embassies and social media. Tibetan advocate groups say information on the Tibetan side of the border remains heavily restricted.

On 30 August, Tibetan police reported that 10 people had been punished for spreading what authorities called “false information” about the scale of the disaster online.

“This crackdown is obstructing not just public reporting of the disaster and relief efforts but the basic work of establishing whether communities are alive and receiving the support that they need,” said Tencho Gyatso, president of the US-based Tibetan advocacy group the International Campaign for Tibet (ICT)

“Sources are now afraid to speak to outside groups including ICT. One source told ICT it was “extremely unsafe” to speak. Another asked us not to make further contact given the potential ramifications,” she said.

View image in fullscreen A press conference held Gyirong after the Nepal-Tibet disaster. Photograph: China News Service/Getty Images

Fan says she is mainly relying on information from Nepal.

“Everyone seems to have forgotten about the workers on the Syaphrubesi–Rasuwagadhi Highway project … All the news coverage is about the hydropower station [in Nepal].

Families of foreign tourists who went missing in Tibet are also desperately searching for information,

View image in fullscreen Sridhar Avvari. Photograph: Supplied

British nationals Sridhar Avvari, 43, his wife, Deepti, 41, and their 14-year-old son Abhinav went missing near the immigration area at Gyirong on 26 August, close to the Nepal-Tibet border. The family lives in India and relatives believe they over on to the Tibetan side.

In a call to the family days earlier, Deepti Avvari told them that there would be no signal but would talk when she returned to an area with network activity. After the flash flood, calls to Deepti’s phone stopped connecting.

“There was no signal, so we can’t talk … After coming down, I will call you again,” Deepti told Priyanka Rapaka, her sister in law.

They are desperately waiting for updates.

View image in fullscreen Deepti Avvari is among the missing. Photograph: Supplied

“We didn’t get any information from China … We are checking online only who are rescued and … how many are dead,” Rapaka said.

View image in fullscreen British national Neetu Goyal Tiwari. Photograph: Supplied

Chinese authorities say they are now able to reach the main disaster zone by road. According to state media they are describing the region as an active search and rescue operation and are searching for hundreds of missing people.

Naresh Goyal is anxiously waiting for news about his sister, Neetu Goyal Tiwari, a 51-year-old missing British national who flew from India to Kathmandu on 14 August to join an Isha Foundation pilgrimage.

“The last message received is that they have reached Gyirong immigration office. “They said they are going to check out.” He says he found his sister’s name on a list of missing people circulating on social media, but said he is unsure where the list originated. Getting information out of the Chinese authorities has been difficult.

“Whenever we ask the China government, they are telling us that they will update us through the embassy of the UK,” he says.

“It is very painful here Now we have spent at least seven days and every minute we are waiting,” Goyal says.

नरेश गोयल अपन बहिन नीतू गोयल तिवारी 51 वर्षीय लापता ब्रिटिश नागरिक के खबर के बेचैनी स इंतजार क रहल छथि जे 14 अगस्त कए इशा फाउंडेशन क तीर्थयात्रा मे शामिल हेबा लेल भारत स काठमांडू पहुंचल छल।

“अंतिम संदेश भेटल अछि जे ओ सब ग्यरोंग इमिग्रेशन ऑफिस पहुँचि गेल छथि, “ओ सब कहलक जे ओ सब चेक आउट करय जा रहल छथि।” हुनकऽ कहना छै कि सोशल मीडिया प॑ घूमी रहलऽ लापता लोगऽ के सूची म॑ हुनका अपनऽ बहिन केरऽ नाम मिललै, लेकिन हुनी कहलकै कि हुनका ई बात के अनिश्चितता छै कि ई सूची कत॑ स॑ निकललऽ छै । चीनी अधिकारी स जानकारी लेब मुश्किल रहल अछि।

ओ कहैत छथि जे जखन-जखन हम चीन सरकार स पूछैत छी त ओ हमरा सब कए कहि रहल अछि जे ओ हमरा सब कए यूके क दूतावास क माध्यम स अपडेट करत।

गोयल कहैत छथि जे एतय बहुत दर्द होइत अछि आब हम सब कम स कम सात दिन बिता देलहुं अछि आ हर मिनट हम सब इंतजार क रहल छी।

title: Caritas Nepal head: Climate change’s toll on Nepal’s people is a ‘profound injustice’ - OSV News
description: Caritas Nepal head: Climate change’s toll on Nepal’s people is a ‘profound injustice’  OSV News
publisher.title: OSV News
full_article:
(OSV News) — Caritas Nepal’s leader is urging global action on climate justice after catastrophic flooding in Nepal claimed more than 1,100 lives and left thousands missing.

Sister Cecilia Durga Shrestha, of the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Joseph of Cluny, stressed that for people who have contributed “very little” to the climate crisis in the world to suffer “disproportionately” from its consequences is “profound injustice.”

The first woman to head Caritas Nepal, she has been leading the organization since 2023 and spoke to OSV News just as the Vatican’s International Theological Commission called for ecological conversion due to “sin against creation and the Creator.”

Sister Cecilia urged “shared responsibility” and said the time has come for “concrete action” to prevent such tragedies from happening.

The Vatican’s commission explained that by failing to care for “our Common Home” with sufficient wisdom and long-term vision, “we not only fail to respect God’s plan and mistreat creation, but we also harm our neighbors, especially the poorest and future generations.”

Devastating floods along Nepal’s border with China

On Aug. 26, the mountain nation of Nepal faced a devastating flash flood along its border with China. According to the National Disaster Risk Management Authority of the South Asian country, around 4,500 people are still missing, and approximately 12,000 have been rescued.

Sister Cecilia told OSV News Sept. 3 that “many of those rescued are currently receiving medical treatment in hospitals and are recovering from their injuries and trauma.”

“Beyond these figures, thousands of families have lost their homes, livelihoods, land, property, and, most painfully, their loved ones,” she said. “The full extent of the impact is still being assessed.”

A woman holds a shovel as she stands inside her damaged shop at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot region Sept. 4, 2026, a week after deadly flash floods and mudslides. (OSV News photo/Adnan Abidi, Reuters)

She said the immediate priority is to “ensure the safety and protection of displaced families, including identifying and allocating safe land for temporary shelter and, where necessary, permanent resettlement,” for which the government of Nepal is responsible.

Government ‘needs to support’ affected communities

“At the same time, the government needs to support affected communities to restore their livelihoods and begin planning for early recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction,” she said.

But the official bodies also “cannot do this alone.”

“With coordinated support from national and international organizations, civil society organizations, development partners and generous international solidarity, I believe Nepal can move towards recovery and rebuild the affected communities with greater resilience,” Sister Cecilia emphasized.

Caritas Nepal, she said, works “hand in hand with the government, complementing its efforts through financial and technical support, humanitarian expertise, coordination and community mobilization.”

“Caritas Nepal can also help ensure that assistance reaches the most vulnerable and affected communities, while supporting early recovery and longer-term rehabilitation in close coordination with government authorities at both national and local levels,” Sister Cecilia said.

The tragedy was a grim confirmation of warnings given earlier this year regarding the effects of climate change on nearby glaciers — the seismic event was caused by a 5.2 magnitude glacial collapse.

Glaciers melting at an accelerating rate

In March, researchers from the International Center for Integrated Mountain Development, or ICIMOD, released a report revealing that glaciers across the Himalayas were melting at an accelerating rate and warned that concrete action was needed to avoid further disasters to communities in the area.

“I believe this is an important question of climate justice and shared responsibility,” Sister Cecilia said.

“Look at Nepal today. High in the Himalayas, our communities are experiencing the devastating consequences of a changing climate. The disaster has swept away homes, land, livelihoods, property and, most painfully, the lives of thousands of people. The question we must ask is: Who is responsible for the suffering of these innocent and vulnerable people? Certainly, it is not the people of Nepal,” she said.

Kamala Bhattarai, wife of Pushpa Raj Bhattarai, 46, who died in deadly flash floods and a mudslide, mourns during a cremation ritual in Kathmandu, Nepal, Sept. 3, 2026, on the premises of Pashupatinath Temple. His body remained missing so a symbolic effigy was used in the ritual. (OSV News photo/Adnan Abidi, Reuters)

Caritas Nepal head stressed that the country contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, “yet our people are among those experiencing severe impacts of climate change. This is a profound injustice.”

“As a development worker and as a Catholic religious sister, I believe we must move beyond discussions and declarations and take concrete action for climate justice,” she said, “particularly for communities and countries that have contributed very little to the climate crisis but are suffering disproportionately from its consequences.”

Time for ‘climate justice and concrete action’

Asked whether developed countries should compensate Nepal for this loss, she replied: “I am not sure that the word ‘compensation’ fully captures what is needed. What I strongly believe is that this is the time for climate justice and concrete action.”

Developed countries, she stressed, “should not only participate in conferences and international conventions; they must translate their commitments into immediate and meaningful action. This should include stronger climate action, adequate climate finance, support for adaptation and resilience, and assistance to vulnerable countries facing climate-related disasters.”

Sister Cecilia said that Nepal needs “international solidarity not only for the immediate humanitarian response, but also for recovery, reconstruction, adaptation and building climate-resilient communities.”

Survivor Sanjay Sah is carried by members of a search and rescue team after they rescued him and another person trapped inside a tunnel in Rasuwa, Nepal, Sept. 4, 2026. They were located at the Upper Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project following devastating floods and mudslides that struck the Bhotekoshi River. (OSV News photo/Nepal Army/Handout via Reuters)

“The people of Nepal should not have to pay with their lives for a crisis to which they have contributed so little. This is a moment for the international community to act with greater responsibility, solidarity, and justice,” she said.

‘Painful reminder” climate change is reality

This disaster, Sister Cecilia said, is a “painful reminder that climate change is not a distant threat — it is a reality affecting people’s lives today. Climate justice is not charity; it is a matter of justice and a right of vulnerable communities.”

“Justice delayed is justice denied,” she stressed, “and we cannot afford to wait while vulnerable people continue to pay the highest price for a crisis they did little to create.”

Caritas Nepal, she said, is currently providing food and non-food assistance, water, sanitation, and hygiene support, and other essential humanitarian needs.

“At the same time, we are looking beyond the immediate emergency towards early recovery, rehabilitation and long-term reconstruction, with a strong focus on ‘building back better.’ Caritas Nepal has significant experience in this area, including its contribution to the recovery and reconstruction efforts following the 2015 earthquake,” Sister Cecilia told OSV News.

Caritas Nepal ‘deeply grateful to our partners’

The sister emphasized that Caritas Nepal is “deeply grateful to our partners, donor organizations, and the Catholic Church for standing with Nepal at this very difficult time. We sincerely appreciate their solidarity, generous contributions and continued commitment to the people of Nepal.”

She appealed for the partners of the Church’s biggest charity organization “to remain engaged beyond the immediate response and support early recovery, rehabilitation, reconstruction and resilient rebuilding.”

The goal, she said, “should not simply be to rebuild what has been lost, but to build back better, safer and more resilient communities.”

“Nepal needs solidarity — not only for emergency relief, but also for recovery, resilience, and a safer and more sustainable future.”

Stephan Rozario writes for OSV News from Dhaka, Bangladesh.

क्लूनी केरऽ सेंट जोसेफ केरऽ सिस्टर्स केरऽ मंडली केरऽ बहिन सेसिलिया दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ न॑ जोर देलकै कि दुनिया केरऽ जलवायु संकट म॑ “बहुत कम” योगदान दै वाला लोगऽ लेली एकरऽ परिणाम स॑ “अननुपातिक रूप स॑” पीड़ित होना “गहन अन्याय” छै ।

बहिन सेसिलिया न॑ “साझा जिम्मेदारी” के आग्रह करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि ऐसनऽ त्रासदी नै होबै लेली “ठोस कार्रवाई” के समय आबी गेलऽ छै ।

वेटिकन केरऽ आयोग न॑ बतैलकै कि पर्याप्त बुद्धि आरू दीर्घकालिक दृष्टि के साथ “हमरऽ साझा घर” के देखभाल नै करला स॑ “हम न सिर्फ भगवान केरऽ योजना के सम्मान करै म॑ विफल रहै छियै आरू सृष्टि के साथ दुर्व्यवहार करै छियै, बल्कि हम्मं॑ अपनऽ पड़ोसी खास करी क॑ सबसें गरीब आरू आबै वाला पीढ़ी क॑ भी नुकसान पहुँचै छियै।”

26 अगस्त कए पहाड़ी राष्ट्र नेपाल कए चीन क संग अपन सीमा पर विनाशकारी फ्लैश फ्लड क सामना करय पड़ल। दक्षिण एशियाई देश केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण के अनुसार, लगभग ४,५०० लोग अखनी तलक लापता छै, आरू लगभग १२,००० लोगऽ क॑ बचालऽ गेलऽ छै ।

बहिन सेसिलिया न॑ ओएसवी न्यूज क॑ ३ सितंबर क॑ बतैलकै कि “बचलऽ गेलऽ लोगऽ म॑ स॑ बहुत लोगऽ क॑ फिलहाल अस्पताल म॑ चिकित्सा के इलाज करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै आरू वू अपनऽ चोट आरू आघात स॑ ठीक होय रहलऽ छै ।”

ओ कहली जे एहि आंकड़ा स आगू हजारों परिवार अपन घर, रोजी-रोटी, जमीन, संपत्ति आ सबस बेसी दर्दनाक बात जे अपन प्रियजन कए गंवा चुकल अछि। “प्रभाव केरऽ पूरा विस्तार केरऽ आकलन अखनी भी करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।”

नेपाल केरऽ नुवाकोट क्षेत्र केरऽ देवीघाट म॑ अपनऽ क्षतिग्रस्त दोकान के भीतर खड़ा होय क॑ एगो महिला फावड़ा पकड़ी क॑ घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ आरू कीचड़ केरऽ स्खलन के एक सप्ताह बाद ४ सितम्बर २०२६ क॑ । (ओएसवी न्यूज फोटो/अदनान अबिदी, रायटर)

ओ कहली जे तत्काल प्राथमिकता अछि जे “विस्थापित परिवार क सुरक्षा आ सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करब, जाहि मे अस्थायी आश्रय आ जरूरत पड़ला पर स्थायी पुनर्वास लेल सुरक्षित जमीन क पहचान आ आवंटन शामिल अछि,” जेकर जिम्मेदारी नेपाल सरकार अछि।

सरकार कें प्रभावित समुदायक कें ‘समर्थन कें जरूरत छै’

ओ कहली जे एकर संग-संग सरकार कए प्रभावित समुदाय कए हुनकर आजीविका कए बहाल करबा लेल मदद करबाक जरूरत अछि आ जल्दी ठीक हेबाक, पुनर्वास आ पुनर्निर्माण क योजना शुरू करबाक जरूरत अछि।

मुदा सरकारी निकाय सेहो “ई काज असगर नहि क’ सकैत अछि।”

सिस्टर सेसिलिया जोर दैत कहलनि जे, राष्ट्रीय आ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठन, नागरिक समाज संगठन, विकास भागीदार आ उदार अंतर्राष्ट्रीय एकजुटता के समन्वित सहयोग स हमरा विश्वास अछि जे नेपाल पुनर्प्राप्ति दिस बढ़ि सकैत अछि आ प्रभावित समुदाय के बेसी लचीलापन के संग पुनर्निर्माण क सकैत अछि।

कैरिटास नेपाल, ओ कहलनि जे, “सरकार के संग हाथ मिला क काज करैत अछि, आर्थिक आ तकनीकी सहयोग, मानवीय विशेषज्ञता, समन्वय आ सामुदायिक जुटान के माध्यम स ओकर प्रयास के पूरक अछि।”

सिस्टर सेसिलिया कहलकै, “कैरिटास नेपाल ई सुनिश्चित करै मँ भी मदद करी सकै छै कि सहायता सबसें कमजोर आरू प्रभावित समुदाय तलक पहुँचै, जबकि राष्ट्रीय आरू स्थानीय दोनों स्तर प सरकारी प्राधिकारी सिनी के साथ घनिष्ठ समन्वय स॑ जल्दी ठीक होय आरू दीर्घकालिक पुनर्वास के समर्थन करी सकै छै ।

ई त्रासदी ई साल केरऽ शुरू म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ नजदीकी ग्लेशियरऽ प॑ पड़ै वाला प्रभाव के संबंध म॑ देलऽ गेलऽ चेतावनी के भयावह पुष्टि छेलै — ई भूकंपीय घटना ५.२ परिमाण के हिमनदी गिरै के कारण बनलऽ छै ।

तेज गति स पिघलैत ग्लेशियर

मार्च म॑ इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट यानी आईसीआईएमओडी केरऽ शोधकर्ता न॑ एगो रिपोर्ट जारी करी क॑ ई बात के खुलासा करलकै कि पूरा हिमालय केरऽ ग्लेशियर तेजी स॑ पिघली रहलऽ छै आरू चेतावनी देल॑ छेलै कि ई क्षेत्र केरऽ समुदायऽ क॑ आरू आपदा स॑ बचै लेली ठोस कार्रवाई के जरूरत छै ।

बहिन सेसिलिया न॑ कहलकै कि हमरऽ मानना ​​छै कि ई जलवायु न्याय आरू साझा जिम्मेदारी केरऽ एगो महत्वपूर्ण सवाल छै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, आइ नेपाल दिस देखू।हिमालयक ऊँच स्थान पर हमर समुदाय बदलैत जलवायु के विनाशकारी परिणाम के अनुभव क रहल अछि।आपदा घर, जमीन, रोजी-रोटी, संपत्ति आ सबस बेसी दर्दनाक बात जे हजारों लोक के जान ल गेल अछि।हमरा सब के जे सवाल पूछय पड़त ओ अछि जे एहि निर्दोष आ कमजोर लोक के दुख के जिम्मेदार के अछि? निश्चित रूप स, इ नहि अछि नेपालक जनता केँ।'

पशुपतिनाथ मन्दिर परिसरमे नेपालक काठमाण्डौमे ३ सितम्बर २०२६ मे घातक झटका बाढ़ि आ कीचड़मे मृत्यु भेल ४६ वर्षीय पुष्पराज भट्टराईक पत्नी कमला भट्टराई । हुनक शरीर गायब रहल तेँ संस्कार मे प्रतीकात्मक मूर्तिक प्रयोग कयल गेल । (ओएसवी न्यूज फोटो/अदनान अबिदी, रायटर)

कैरिटास नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख न॑ जोर देलकै कि ई देश वैश्विक ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन म॑ ०.१% स॑ भी कम योगदान दै छै, “तभियो भी हमरऽ लोग जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ गंभीर प्रभाव के अनुभव करै वाला म॑ शामिल छै । ई गहींर अन्याय अछि।”

हुनी कहलकै, “एक विकास कार्यकर्ता के रूप मँ आरू कैथोलिक धार्मिक बहिन के रूप मँ हमरऽ मानना ​​छै कि हमरा सब क॑ चर्चा आरू घोषणा स॑ आगू बढ़ी क॑ जलवायु न्याय लेली ठोस कार्रवाई करना चाहियऽ, खास करी क॑ वू समुदाय आरू देशऽ लेली जे जलवायु संकट म॑ बहुत कम योगदान देल॑ छै लेकिन एकरऽ परिणाम स॑ असमान रूप स॑ पीड़ित छै ।”

‘जलवायु न्याय एवं ठोस कार्यवाही’ के समय |

विकसित देश कए एहि नुकसान क भरपाई नेपाल कए करबाक चाही कि नहि, एहि पर ओ जवाब देलथि जे हमरा यकीन नहि अछि जे ‘मुआवजा’ शब्द मे जे जरूरत अछि ओकरा पूरा तरह स समेटल गेल अछि। हमरऽ दृढ़ विश्वास छै कि ई समय जलवायु न्याय आरू ठोस कार्रवाई के छै।”

विकसित देशऽ क॑ हुनी जोर देलकै कि “केवल सम्मेलन आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अधिवेशन म॑ ही नै भाग लेना चाहियऽ; हुनका अपनऽ प्रतिबद्धता क॑ तत्काल आरू सार्थक कार्य म॑ बदलना चाहियऽ । एहि मे जलवायु संबंधी मजबूत कार्रवाई, पर्याप्त जलवायु वित्त, अनुकूलन आ लचीलापन कें समर्थन, आ जलवायु सं संबंधित आपदाक कें सामना करय वाला कमजोर देशक कें सहायता शामिल होबाक चाही.”

बहिन सेसिलिया न॑ कहलकै कि नेपाल क॑ “तत्काल मानवीय प्रतिक्रिया लेली ही नै, बल्कि पुनर्प्राप्ति, पुनर्निर्माण, अनुकूलन आरू जलवायु-लचीली समुदाय के निर्माण लेली भी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय एकजुटता के जरूरत छै ।”

नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा म॑ ४ सितम्बर २०२६ क॑ सुरंग के भीतर फंसलऽ एगो दोसरऽ व्यक्ति क॑ बचाबै के बाद बची गेलऽ संजय साह क॑ खोजबीन आरू बचाव टीम के सदस्य न॑ ल॑ जाय रहलऽ छै । (ओएसवी न्यूज फोटो/नेपाल सेना/हैण्डआउट रायटर के माध्यम स)

ओ कहलनि जे, जाहि संकट मे हुनकर योगदान एतेक कम अछि, ओहि संकट मे नेपालक जनता केँ अपन जान सँ भुगतान नहि करय पड़य। ई अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय लेली एगो ऐसनऽ क्षण छै कि वू अधिक जिम्मेदारी, एकजुटता, आरू न्याय के साथ काम करै ।'

‘दर्दनाक स्मरण” जलवायु परिवर्तन यथार्थ अछि |

बहिन सेसिलिया न॑ कहलकै कि ई आपदा एगो “एक दर्दनाक याद दिलाबै छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन दूर के खतरा नै छै — ई एगो वास्तविकता छै जे आज लोगऽ के जीवन क॑ प्रभावित करी रहलऽ छै ।जलवायु न्याय दान नै छै;ई न्याय के बात छै आरू कमजोर समुदाय के अधिकार छै।”

ओ जोर दैत कहलनि जे, न्याय मे देरी न्याय स वंचित अछि, आ हम सब इंतजार नहि क सकैत छी, जखन कि कमजोर लोक एहन संकट क सबस बेसी कीमत चुकाबैत रहथि, जेकरा पैदा करबा मे ओ बहुत कम काज केलथि।

कैरिटास नेपाल एखन खाद्य आ गैर-खाद्य सहायता, पानि, स्वच्छता, आ स्वच्छता सहायता, आ अन्य आवश्यक मानवीय आवश्यकता उपलब्ध करा रहल अछि ।

सिस्टर सेसिलिया न॑ ओएसवी न्यूज स॑ कहलकै कि एकरऽ साथ ही हम्मं॑ तत्काल आपातकाल स॑ आगू बढ़ी क॑ जल्दी ठीक होय, पुनर्वास आरू दीर्घकालिक पुनर्निर्माण के तरफ देखै छियै, जेकरा म॑ ‘बिल्ड बैक बेटर’ प॑ मजबूत ध्यान देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

कैरिटास नेपाल ‘अपन साझेदारक प्रति गहींर आभारी’

बहिन न॑ जोर देलकै कि कैरिटास नेपाल “हमरऽ साथी, दाता संगठन, आरू कैथोलिक चर्च केरऽ गहराई स॑ आभारी छै कि ई बहुत कठिन समय म॑ नेपाल के साथ खड़ा छै । हम्मं॑ हुनकऽ एकजुटता, उदार योगदान आरू नेपाल केरऽ जनता के प्रति निरंतर प्रतिबद्धता के ईमानदारी स॑ सराहना करै छियै ।”

हुनी चर्च केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ चैरिटी संगठन केरऽ भागीदारऽ स॑ अपील करलकै कि “तत्काल प्रतिक्रिया स॑ परे जुटलऽ रह॑ आरू जल्दी ठीक होय, पुनर्वास, पुनर्निर्माण आरू लचीला पुनर्निर्माण के समर्थन करै ।”

हुनी कहलकै कि लक्ष्य खाली जे कुछ हेराय गेलऽ छै ओकरा दोबारा बनाना नै होना चाहियऽ, बल्कि बेहतर, सुरक्षित आरू अधिक लचीला समुदाय क॑ वापस बनाबै के होना चाहियऽ ।”

“नेपाल क॑ एकजुटता के जरूरत छै — न सिर्फ आपातकालीन राहत लेली, बल्कि ठीक होय, लचीलापन, आरू सुरक्षित आरू अधिक टिकाऊ भविष्य लेली भी।”

full_article:
Geoff Bennett:

In the day's other headlines: a pair of miraculous rescues in Nepal's flood zone. Two men were pulled from a tunnel more than a week after the catastrophic deluge that barreled through Himalayan river valleys. It's given first responders hope as they continue their search that others might also be alive.

Stephanie Sy has more.

Stephanie Sy:

From beneath the mounds of mud and debris, a miracle.

(Cheering)

(Applause)

Stephanie Sy:

Two workers who had been trapped in the underground tunnels of a hydropower plant for nine days were found alive. Search teams said they heard voices from inside the tunnel, allowing them to pinpoint the two men. Both were airlifted to a hospital in nearby Kathmandu. One of them, officials say, is in critical condition.

But Sanjay Sah had enough strength to speak, telling an army rescuer:

Sanjay Sah, Rescue Worker (through interpreter):

I was working as an operator in the control room. Since I was in the control room, my responsibility was to save everyone's lives. After such an accident happened, I could not just run away alone.

Stephanie Sy:

The workers' families, who had waited anxiously for days, said they were ready to give up hope when the news came.

Hira Shova Maharjan, Wife of Rescued Worker (through interpreter): We are very happy. Every day and night, we have been waiting, and even today we didn't even believe that he would come back. When I saw his picture in the news, we were so happy. All of us were crying.

Stephanie Sy:

For more than a week, crews have crawled through harrowing, tight spaces underground, looking and listening for any signs of life in the system of a dozen massive hydropower tunnels and navigating around tons of water and debris.

Rescue crews are working on the assumption that there are more survivors. More than 100 others are thought to be trapped in the same tunnel where the two men were found. So far, at least 1,200 people have been confirmed dead from last week's devastating floods, and more than 5,000 remain missing.

For the "PBS News Hour," I'm Stephanie Sy.

Geoff Bennett:

Also today, Ukraine's president says a Russian drone struck the headquarters of the country's security service today, wounding at least nine people. Heavy black smoke poured from the window of the agency's office in Central Kyiv. It's one of the most high-profile targets to be hit so far in the war.

Ukraine's foreign minister called the strike a major escalation, and President Zelenskyy says the military will retaliate in kind. Just outside the capital, another drone attack destroyed this warehouse as the city continues to face round-the-clock bombing.

One newlywed couple said that, despite the attacks, life must go on.

Iryna Baranova, Kyiv, Ukraine, Resident (through interpreter):

In the morning, when I was returning home from hair and makeup, I was returning during the sounds of explosions. But thank God everything was fine. Two explosions were heard. The alarm ended. We got together and went to the registration ceremony.

Geoff Bennett:

Meantime, on the diplomatic front, President Zelenskyy confirmed in a video today that U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Moscow and then Kyiv for talks on Sunday.

President Trump tried to downplay the severity of the war in Iran today. Speaking with reporters in the Oval Office, he was asked about comments yesterday from J.D. Vance, in which the vice president said he -- quote -- "wouldn't call it a war."

In response, Mr. Trump largely agreed, saying that the U.S. is carrying out what he called intermittent strikes.

President Donald Trump:

A lot of people don't call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us. It's not a big thing.

Geoff Bennett:

At least 18 U.S. service members have died and hundreds more have been wounded since the U.S. and Israel first launched military strikes on Iran more than six months ago.

A cleanup is under way across parts of the Midwest and East Coast after severe storms swept through overnight and into today, toppling trees and leaving thousands without power. In Ohio, crews carried out water rescues after floodwaters swamped residential neighborhoods, while, in Pittsburgh, a flood watch remains in effect after the city saw more than two inches of rainfall overnight.

Meantime, in and around Washington, D.C., the National Weather Service issued severe thunderstorm and flash flood warnings amid a cluster of storms that shook the area just before midnight. Local media is reporting that lightning flashes hit the ground every second for several minutes in some areas.

In New York, police fatally shot a man wielding a knife on the city's iconic Brooklyn Bridge early this morning. Footage shows a large police response after officers responded to a call of a man walking on the beams of the structure. Authorities say that police harnessed themselves to the bridge and tried to convince the man to come down for nearly an hour, before he came at them with a knife.

Gerard Dowling, NYPD Emergency Services Unit:

They observed that the male was holding a knife and he stated to them: "I want to die. I want you to kill me. I have a bomb. You're not going to make me do something bad to the cops."

Geoff Bennett:

It is the second time this week that New York police have taken deadly action towards a knife-wielding suspect. On Monday, officers shot and killed a woman who had stabbed two people in Times Square, one of them fatally.

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert says she's stepping down at the end of the year after more than seven years at the helm of the league. In a statement, she writes -- quote -- "I retire knowing we have built something bigger, stronger, and more enduring than we could have imagined."

During her tenure, the WNBA has seen record TV ratings and attendance, fueled in large part by stars like Caitlin Clark and A'ja Wilson, along with expansion and the league's first million-dollar player salaries. But Engelbert has been criticized by some players for her leadership, especially on matters such as pay, officiating, and the league's handling of player concerns. No plans for a successor have been announced.

On Wall Street today, stocks ended lower amid renewed concerns about higher interest rates. The Dow Jones industrial average lost about 270 points. The Nasdaq fell nearly a third-of-1-percent. The S&P 500 also ended the week a bit lower.

एक सप्ताह स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ चालक दल जमीन के नीचे के दुखद, तंग जगहऽ म॑ रेंगतें हुअ॑ एक दर्जन विशाल जलविद्युत सुरंगऽ के सिस्टम म॑ जीवन केरऽ कोय भी संकेत देखै आरू सुनै छै आरू टन पानी आरू मलबा के आसपास घूमी रहलऽ छै ।

बचाव दल एहि धारणा पर काज क रहल अछि जे एहि ठाम बचि गेल लोक बेसी अछि। मानल जा रहल अछि जे, जाहि सुरंग मे दुनू गोटे भेटल छल, ओहि सुरंग मे 100 स बेसी लोक फंसल छथि। पिछला सप्ताह के विनाशकारी बाढ़ि सं एखन धरि कम सं कम 1200 लोक के मौत के पुष्टि भ चुकल अछि, आओर 5000 सं बेसि लोक लापता अछि.

"पीबीएस न्यूज आवर" के लेल, हम स्टेफनी साइ छी।

जॉफ बेनेट : १.

साथ ही आय यूक्रेन केरऽ राष्ट्रपति के कहना छै कि आय रूसी ड्रोन न॑ देश केरऽ सुरक्षा सेवा केरऽ मुख्यालय प॑ हमला करी क॑ कम स॑ कम नौ लोग घायल होय गेलै । सेंट्रल कीव मे एजेंसी के ऑफिस के खिड़की सं भारी कारी धुआं बहल. ई युद्ध म॑ अब तलक के सबसें हाई प्रोफाइल निशाना म॑ स॑ एक छै ।

यूक्रेन केरऽ विदेश मंत्री न॑ ई हड़ताल क॑ एगो बड़ऽ बढ़ोत्तरी बतैलकै आरू राष्ट्रपति जेलेन्स्की के कहना छै कि सेना भी एकरऽ बदला लेतै । राजधानी केरऽ ठीक बाहर एगो आरू ड्रोन हमला न॑ ई गोदाम क॑ तबाह करी देलकै, कैन्हेंकि शहर म॑ चौबीसों घंटा बमबारी के सामना करना जारी छै ।

एकटा नवविवाहित जोड़ी कहलनि जे, हमलाक बादो जीवन आगू बढ़य पड़त।

इरीना बरनोवा, कीव, यूक्रेन, निवासी (दुभाषिया के माध्यम से):

भोरे जखन केश आ मेकअप स घर घुरैत रही त विस्फोटक आवाज के दौरान वापस आबि रहल छलहुं। मुदा भगवानक शुक्र जे सब किछु ठीक छल। दू टा विस्फोटक आवाज सुनबा मे आयल। अलार्म समाप्त भ गेल। हम सभ एकठाम भ' क' रजिस्ट्रेशन समारोह मे चलि गेलहुँ।

जॉफ बेनेट : १.

ई बीच कूटनीतिक मोर्चा प॑ राष्ट्रपति जेलेन्स्की न॑ आय एगो वीडियो म॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि अमेरिकी वार्ताकार स्टीव विटकोफ आरू जेरेड कुशनर रविवार क॑ बातचीत लेली मास्को आरू ओकरा बाद कीव के दौरा करतै ।

राष्ट्रपति ट्रंप न॑ आय ईरान म॑ युद्ध केरऽ गंभीरता क॑ कम करै के कोशिश करलकै । ओवल ऑफिस में पत्रकार सब सं बात करैत हुनका सं काल्हि जे.डी.वैंस के टिप्पणी के बारे में पूछल गेल छल, जाहि में उपराष्ट्रपति कहलनि जे ओ -- उद्धरण -- "एकरा युद्ध नहिं कहताह."

एकरऽ जवाब म॑ श्री ट्रंप न॑ काफी हद तलक सहमत होय क॑ कहलकै कि अमेरिका जेकरा क॑ हुनी रुक-रुक क॑ हमला कहलकै ।

राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प : १.

बहुत लोक एकरा युद्ध नहि कहैत छथि। हम एकरा सैन्य संघर्ष कहैत छी, कारण ई हमरा सभक लेल छोट-छोट आलू अछि। ई कोनो पैघ बात नहि।

जॉफ बेनेट : १.

छह महीना स॑ भी अधिक समय पहल॑ अमेरिका आरू इजरायल न॑ ईरान प॑ पहलऽ बार सैन्य हमला करला के बाद स॑ कम स॑ कम १८ अमेरिकी सेवा सदस्यऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू सैकड़ों लोग घायल होय गेलऽ छै ।

रात भर आरू आय तलक भयंकर तूफान के बाद मध्य पश्चिम आरू पूर्वी तट के कुछ हिस्सा म॑ सफाई चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ गाछ गिरी गेलऽ छै आरू हजारों लोगऽ क॑ बिजली के कमी होय गेलऽ छै । ओहियो म॑ बाढ़ के पानी न॑ आवासीय मोहल्ला म॑ दलदली होय के बाद चालक दल न॑ पानी के बचाव के काम करलकै, जबकि पिट्सबर्ग म॑ शहर म॑ रात भर दू इंच स॑ भी अधिक बारिश के बाद बाढ़ केरऽ निगरानी लागू छै ।

एम्हर वाशिंगटन डी.सी. स्थानीय मीडिया के खबर अछि जे किछ इलाका मे हर सेकेंड मे बिजली के चमक कई मिनट तक जमीन पर टकराइत अछि.

न्यूयॉर्क म॑ पुलिस न॑ आय सुबह शहर केरऽ प्रतिष्ठित ब्रुकलिन ब्रिज प॑ चाकू चलाबै वाला एगो आदमी क॑ जानलेवा गोली मारलकै । फुटेज मे देखल गेल अछि जे संरचना के बीम पर चलय वाला एकटा आदमी के फोन पर अधिकारी के जवाब देला के बाद पुलिस के बड़का प्रतिक्रिया देखल गेल अछि. अधिकारि सब के कहनाय छनि जे पुलिस पुल पर अपना के जोड़ि लेलक आ करीब एक घंटा धरि ओहि आदमी के नीचा उतरय लेल मनाबय के कोशिश केलक, ताहि सं पहिने ओ चाकू ल क ओकरा पर आबि गेल.

जेरार्ड डाउलिंग, एनवाईपीडी आपातकालीन सेवा इकाई:

ओ सभ देखलक जे नर चाकू पकड़ने छल आ ओ ओकरा सभ केँ बयान देलक: "हम मर' चाहैत छी. हम चाहैत छी जे अहाँ हमरा मारि दियौक. हमरा लग बम अछि. अहाँ सभ हमरा पुलिसक संग कोनो खराब काज नहि कर' जा रहल छी."

जॉफ बेनेट : १.

ई सप्ताह ई दोसरऽ बार छै जब॑ न्यूयॉर्क पुलिस न॑ चाकू धारण करै वाला संदिग्ध के प्रति घातक कार्रवाई करलकै । सोमदिन टाइम्स स्क्वायर मे दू गोटे के चाकू सं हमला करय वाली महिला के अधिकारी गोली मारि क हत्या क देलक, जाहि मे सं एकटा जानलेवा भ गेल।

डब्ल्यूएनबीए केरऽ आयुक्त कैथी एंगेलबर्ट के कहना छै कि लीग केरऽ पतवार प॑ सात साल स॑ भी अधिक समय के बाद साल के अंत म॑ पद छोड़ी रहलऽ छै । एकटा बयान मे ओ लिखैत छथि -- उद्धरण -- "हम ई जानि क' रिटायर भ' जाइत छी जे हम सभ कल्पना सँ बेसी पैघ, मजबूत, आओर स्थायी किछु बनौने छी."

हुनकऽ कार्यकाल के दौरान डब्ल्यूएनबीए न॑ रिकॉर्ड टीवी रेटिंग आरू उपस्थिति देखन॑ छै, जेकरा क॑ बहुत हद तलक कैटलिन क्लार्क आरू अ’जा विल्सन जैसनऽ सितारा के साथ-साथ विस्तार आरू लीग केरऽ पहलऽ मिलियन डॉलर के खिलाड़ी के वेतन स॑ ईंधन मिललऽ छै । लेकिन एंगेलबर्ट क॑ हुनकऽ नेतृत्व लेली कुछ खिलाड़ी न॑ आलोचना करल॑ छै, खास करी क॑ वेतन, पदाधिकारी, आरू लीग द्वारा खिलाड़ी के चिंता क॑ संभालना जैसनऽ मामला प॑ । उत्तराधिकारी के कोनो योजना के घोषणा नै भेल अछि।

वॉल स्ट्रीट पर आई ब्याज दर बढ़ला के फेर सं चिंता के बीच शेयर कम भ गेल. डाउ जोन्स औद्योगिक औसत मे करीब 270 अंक क गिरावट आयल। नैस्डैक मे लगभग एक प्रतिशत क गिरावट दर्ज कैल गेल। एस एंड पी 500 सेहो सप्ताह कनि कम समाप्त केलक।

full_article:
Two workers rescued alive after 9 days



Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.



KATHMANDU: "Hunchha" - yes, we hear you. Just after dawn on Friday, a faint reply became the first voice rescuers had heard from inside the buried Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel since the Aug 26 flood. Nepal army personnel called out, "Brothers, we are a rescue team, we are coming," and heard "Hunchha, hunchha" from the other side. By 9.20am, two workers had been pulled out alive after nine days underground - the first such breakthrough from Nepal's flood-hit hydropower tunnels.The men were identified as mechanical foreman Sanjay Sah, 30, and mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, 45. Sah was stable, while Maharjan was admitted to intensive care. A third person was later found dead inside; officials said the swollen body could not immediately be identified. Officials believe around 41 workers could be trapped in the tunnel.Getting to Friday morning had taken days.When the flood struck around 10am on Aug 26, it buried the Trishuli 3A project under mud, rocks and debris and erased the tunnel entrance from view. A concentrated rescue push began around the fifth day.The powerhouse had three possible approaches - an access tunnel, cable-duct tunnel and tailrace tunnel - and teams chose the cable duct, the shortest route, though it had a steep incline and a sharp 90-degree bend. The entrance itself lay beneath a nearly 30m-high pile of boulders and debris."Soon after the flood, Nepal Army's Special Forces, Combat Engineers and Collapsed Structure Search and Rescue teams were deployed here," Lt Col Ganga Baral, who commanded the operation, said. "Although it took some time to get the result, we eventually succeeded in rescuing two people alive."Inside, the problems multiplied. Mud and rocks, some larger than vehicles, blocked the route. Army engineers used controlled explosives where excavation alone could not clear them. Water had collected further inside, forcing crews to deploy pumps and cut drainage channels towards Trishuli river.Rescuers then found a gap about 1.5 metres wide near the tunnel roof. They worked through it, carving a passage barely large enough for a person while clearing sludge ahead. By Friday morning, Nepal army said teams had reached about 100m inside the tunnel. Australian tunnelling expert Arnold Dix, referring separately to the route towards the underground powerhouse, estimated that rescuers had tunnelled through about 60m and still had roughly 150 metres to go.Dix, who advised the operation, said rescuers faced conditions without precedent. “We knew they would be up ahead, but we didn’t know where exactly. So you just have to start digging in the right direction,” he said. He described the wider rescue effort as something “the world has not seen before”.The seven-storey underground powerhouse offered one reason for hope. Rescue teams found the lower two levels filled with mud while higher sections had retained space, potentially providing air pockets. Oxygen was pumped forward as crews advanced. Then came the voice.Engineer and lawmaker Shriram Neupane, who was involved in the operation, said rescuers first confirmed that more than one person was responding. “The fact that voices were heard from inside was an encouraging sign,” he said.By 9.20am Friday, Sah and Maharjan were out. Baral called it “an almost unbelievable success”. “We worked day and night. We kept at it,” he said. “We have proved that Nepalese can do it too.”The search continued after the celebration. A seven-member specialised team crawled through sections for 15-20 minutes at a stretch, encountering mud, sludge, rocks and collapsed overhead slabs. They found the unidentified body. “We did not hear any other voices,” a rescuer said. By afternoon, teams said they had reached the farthest accessible section, though project engineers were considering another inspection of possible spaces before calling off the tunnel search.Nepal’s disaster authority said the number of bodies recovered stood at 1,294, with 5,053 people missing, as on Friday night.

title: Rescue of Nepal hydropower workers ‘triumph for humans and humanity’, tunnelling expert says - theguardian.com
description: Rescue of Nepal hydropower workers ‘triumph for humans and humanity’, tunnelling expert says  theguardian.com
publisher.title: theguardian.com
full_article:
There is renewed hope amid the devastation wreaked by the flash flooding disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border as the world witnesses “one of the great rescues of the 21st century”.

Nine days after the deadly floods, two workers were pulled out alive from a flooded hydropower tunnel in Nepal.

Sanjay Shah and Kabir Maharajan were rescued from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, more than a week after a glacial collapse created a torrent of mud, water and debris that swept away buildings, roads and bridges along the border between Nepal and China.

Two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after Nepal-Tibet floods Read more

Hundreds more employees who worked in various hydropower projects along the banks of Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers remain missing, but the Australian engineer and geologist Arnold Dix, who was invited by Nepali authorities to advise on the Trishuli 3A operation, says Friday’s successful rescue will help lift spirits.

“We’ve found two people alive, so that gives us hope,” Dix says.

“After more than a week, everyone’s exhausted, but this spurs us on to try even harder and it now also gives us focus for how we might approach other rescues in other locations.

“We now have proof that people can survive this long.”

View image in fullscreen Arnold Dix at the site of the Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel collapse, in Uttarakhand, India in 2023. All 41 workers were rescued. Photograph: Harish Tyagi/EPA

Dix has previously assisted at other disaster sites such as the 2023 Silkyara tunnel operation, where all 41 workers were rescued after a tunnel collapsed in India, and the tunnels of Ground Zero after 9/11.

But with almost 30 hydropower projects reported damaged, the Nepal floods are unlike any other disaster he has worked on.

“Normally, I deal with a single disaster – this is 27 concurrently,” he says.

On his specific rescue operation, workers had already had trouble identifying the location of Trishuli 3A. They then had to work out which tunnel would give access to the power station before the digging could begin.

But as the process began, rocks the size of vehicles blocked rescuers, forcing them to use explosives. This isn’t the preferred method, as it can pose risks to those on the other side, Dix says.

When they reached the tunnel, rescuers found it was full of water, forcing them to dig an emergency trench to try to drain it. They worried the workers inside could have already drowned, but on Friday morning about 50 metres in, they reported hearing a faint voice.

The team called out, “Don’t panic, we are rescuing you.” From inside the tunnel a voice replied: “OK.”

Watching the video of the men pulled from the tunnel alive reminds Dix of why he does this.

“We do it because we’re decent human beings and that’s what human beings do: help one another,” he says.

“This is a real triumph for humans and humanity.”

0:51 Workers pulled alive from hydropower tunnel nine days after Nepal flood disaster – video

Another 40 workers are believed to be trapped inside Trishuli 3A and rescuers face significant risks. If there is water in the tunnel ahead of the team and they break rock, they could drown, and as they are now below flood-plain level, water could also inundate rescuers from behind.

“Yes, we have the reward of having rescued two people now, but we have to be so careful,” Dix says.

“The team’s lives are at risk right now and if they can’t get out in time they will drown.

“Like, this is not a drill, we are witnessing one of the great rescues of the 21st century.”

The rescue team was on Friday tunnelling to what is known as the “Goldilocks zone” at the top of the 11-storey Trishuli 3A power station, where they are hoping to find more survivors.

More than 270 people have already been rescued from various hydropower projects. At least 1,294 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country’s disaster management agency.

Thirty-eight Australian government officials, disaster response specialists and humanitarian workers are now on the ground in Nepal assisting in search-and-rescue and relief efforts. The latest cohort to arrive – a 15-person Australian Disaster Assistance Response Team – landed in Kathmandu late on Friday night. A further seven disaster victim identification specialists from the federal police will leave Australia on Saturday.

As at 4 September, the Nepali government has reported 1,294 confirmed deaths, while 5,053 people remain missing, including 583 foreign nationals.

As at 5 September, the Chinese government reported 31 confirmed deaths and 531 missing people, with 261 of those being foreign citizens.

हिमनदी गिरला सँ नेपाल आ चीनक सीमा पर बनल भवन, सड़क आ पुल सब के बहरा गेल थाल, पानि आ मलबा के धार बनला के एक सप्ताह स बेसी के बाद शुक्रदिन संजय शाह आ कबीर महाराजन के त्रिशूली 3ए जलविद्युत परियोजना स बचाओल गेल।

नेपाल केरऽ भोटे कोशी आरू त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे विभिन्न जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ काम करै वाला सैकड़ों आरू कर्मचारी अभी भी लापता छै, लेकिन त्रिशुली ३ ए ऑपरेशन के सलाह दै लेली नेपाली अधिकारियऽ द्वारा आमंत्रित करलऽ गेलऽ ऑस्ट्रेलियाई इंजीनियर आरू भूवैज्ञानिक अर्नोल्ड डिक्स के कहना छै कि शुक्रवार क॑ सफल बचाव स॑ मनोबल बढ़ै म॑ मदद मिलतै ।

डिक्स कहैत छथि, “हमरा सभ केँ दू गोटे जीवित भेटल अछि, तेँ एहि सँ हमरा सभ केँ आशा भेटैत अछि.”

“एक सप्ताह स॑ भी अधिक समय बाद सब थक गेलऽ छै, लेकिन ई हमरा सब क॑ आरू कोशिश करै लेली प्रेरित करै छै आरू ई स॑ अब॑ ई बात प॑ भी ध्यान देलऽ जाय छै कि हम्मं॑ दोसरऽ स्थानऽ प॑ दोसरऽ बचाव के कोना संपर्क करी सकै छियै ।

“हमरा सभ लग आब प्रमाण अछि जे लोक एतेक दिन धरि जीबि सकैत अछि।”

फुलस्क्रीन म॑ छवि देखऽ अर्नोल्ड डिक्स न॑ सिल्क्यारा बेंड-बारकोट सुरंग गिरै के जगह प॑, भारत केरऽ उत्तराखंड म॑ २०२३ म॑ ।सब ४१ मजदूरऽ क॑ बचाय लेलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । फोटोग्राफ : हरीश त्यागी/ईपीए

डिक्स न॑ पहल॑ भी अन्य आपदा स्थलऽ प॑ मदद करल॑ छै जेना कि २०२३ केरऽ सिल्क्यारा सुरंग संचालन, जहां भारत म॑ सुरंग गिरला के बाद सब ४१ मजदूरऽ क॑ बचालऽ गेलऽ छेलै, आरू ९/११ के बाद ग्राउंड जीरो केरऽ सुरंगऽ प॑ भी मदद करी चुकलऽ छै ।

लेकिन लगभग ३० जलविद्युत परियोजना क्षतिग्रस्त होय के खबर के साथ नेपाल के बाढ़ि हुनकऽ काम करलऽ गेलऽ कोनो भी आपदा स॑ अलग छै ।

ओ कहैत छथि जे सामान्य तौर पर हम एकटा आपदा स निपटैत छी – इ एक संग 27 अछि।

हुनकऽ विशिष्ट बचाव अभियान प॑ मजदूरऽ क॑ त्रिशुली ३ ए केरऽ स्थान के पहचान करै म॑ पहल॑ स॑ ही परेशानी होय चुकलऽ छेलै । एकरऽ बाद हुनका ई पता लगाबै ल॑ पड़लै कि खुदाई शुरू होय स॑ पहल॑ कोन सुरंग स॑ पावर स्टेशन तलक पहुँच मिलतै ।

लेकिन जेना-जेना ई प्रक्रिया शुरू होलै, गाड़ी के आकार के चट्टान न॑ बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ रोकी देलकै, जेकरा स॑ ओकरा विस्फोटक के इस्तेमाल करै ल॑ मजबूर होय गेलै । डिक्स कहैत छथि जे ई पसंदीदा तरीका नहिं अछि, कारण एहि सं दोसर दिस के लोक के लेल खतरा भ’ सकैत अछि.

जखन ओ सब सुरंग पर पहुंचल त बचावकर्मी कए पता चलल जे इ सुरंग पानि स भरल अछि, जाहि स हुनका सब कए इमरजेंसी खाई खोदबा लेल मजबूर कैल गेल ताकि ओकर पानी निकालबाक कोशिश कैल जा सकए। हुनका सब के चिंता छल जे भीतर के मजदूर पहिने सं डूबि सकैत छल, मुदा शुक्रदिन भोर मे करीब 50 मीटर अंदर, ओ सब मंद आवाज सुनबाक सूचना देलक।

टीम आवाज देलक, “घबराब नहि जाउ, हम अहाँ केँ बचा रहल छी।” सुरंगक भीतरसँ एकटा आवाज उत्तर देलक: “ठीक छै।”

सुरंग स॑ खींचलऽ गेलऽ आदमी सिनी के वीडियो क॑ जिंदा देखला स॑ डिक्स क॑ ई बात के याद आबी जाय छै कि हुनी ऐसनऽ कियैक करै छै ।

ओ कहैत छथि, “हम सभ एहि लेल करैत छी जे हम सभ्य मनुक्ख छी आ मनुक्ख सेहो एहने करैत अछि: एक दोसराक मदद करब.”

“ई मनुष्य आ मानवताक लेल वास्तविक जीत अछि।”

0:51 नेपाल बाढ़िक आपदाक नौ दिनक बाद जलविद्युत सुरंगसँ जिबैत मजदूर खींचल – भिडियो

त्रिशूली 3 ए के भीतर 40 अन्य मजदूर फंसल आ बचाव करय वाला के काफी जोखिम के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि. अगर टीम के आगू सुरंग में पानि छै आ ओ सब चट्टान तोड़ि सकैत छैथ त ओ डूबि सकैत छैथ, आ जेना कि ओ सब आब बाढ़ि के मैदान के स्तर सं नीचा छैथ, पाछू सं बचावकर्ता के सेहो पानि बाढ़ि में आबि सकैत छैथ.

डिक्स कहैत छथि, “हँ, हमरा सभ केँ ई इनाम अछि जे आब दू गोटे केँ बचा लेलहुँ, मुदा हमरा सभ केँ एतेक सावधान रहय पड़त।”

ओ कहलनि जे, टीम के जान एखन खतरा मे अछि आओर अगर समय पर बाहर नहि निकलि सकैत अछि त ओ डूबि जायत.

“जेना, ई कोनो ड्रिल नै छै, हम 21वीं सदी केरऽ एगो महान बचाव के गवाह बनी रहलऽ छियै।”

बचाव टीम शुक्रवार क॑ 11 मंजिला त्रिशुली 3ए पावर स्टेशन केरऽ ऊपरी हिस्सा म॑ “गोल्डिलॉक्स जोन” के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय वाला जगह प॑ सुरंग बनाबै के काम करी रहलऽ छेलै, जहां ओकरा उम्मीद छै कि ओकरा आरू बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ मिलतै ।

विभिन्न जलविद्युत परियोजना स 270 स बेसी लोक कए बचाउल जा चुकल अछि। देश केरऽ आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार बाढ़ म॑ कम स॑ कम १,२९४ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू ५,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै ।

ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ 38 सरकारी अधिकारी, आपदा प्रतिक्रिया विशेषज्ञ आरू मानवीय कार्यकर्ता अब॑ नेपाल म॑ जमीन प॑ मौजूद छै आरू खोज-बचाव आरू राहत कार्य म॑ सहायता करी रहलऽ छै । नवीनतम कोहोर्ट जे आयल छल – 15 गोटेक ऑस्ट्रेलियाई आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम – शुक्रदिन देर राति काठमांडू मे उतरल. संघीय पुलिस केरऽ सात आरू आपदा पीड़ित पहचान विशेषज्ञ शनिदिन ऑस्ट्रेलिया स॑ निकली जैतै ।

४ सितम्बर धरि नेपाली सरकार १ हजार २९४ गोटेके मृत्यु पुष्टि भेल अछि त ५८३ गोटे विदेशी नागरिक सहित ५ हजार ५३ गोटे लापता अछि ।

5 सितंबर तक चीन सरकार 31 पुष्टि भेल मौत आ 531 लोक के लापता होयबाक सूचना देलक अछि, जाहि मे 261 विदेशी नागरिक अछि।
